newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 25.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 25.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 blue chip share index managed to break its six-day losing streak adding over one percent despite a growing conviction among economists that U.S. interest rates are set to rise for the first time in two years. The benchmark index finished 55.9 points higher at 4,270.7, just below the day's best levels.

FRANKFURT - German equities ended bourse just shy of an intraday high, supported by a firm dollar and bund strength, turnover was hit by FOMC meeting this afternoon, dealers say 25 basis point U.S. rate rise to 5.50 percent discounted. The DAX-30 index ended at 3,349.14 up 27.30 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,374.93.

PARIS - French shares closed much higher ahead of an expected decision by the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) to raise U.S. interest rates by 0.25 percentage points, a strong start on Wall Street underpinned the French rise. The CAC-40 index closed 44.97 points or 1.74 percent higher at 2,624.25.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended more than one percent higher in a steady rise, profiting from a strong Wall Street and firming bond futures, the market was expecting the U.S. Fed to raise interest rates by 25 basis points at a meeting the same day of the policy making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). The broad Swiss Performance Index closed up 31.18 points or 1.09 percent to 2,887.96.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks bounced higher, propelled by buy-backs following a tumble of over three percent the previous day which was triggered by a government official's remarks about the possibility of a further rise in the national sales tax. The 225-share Nikkei average finished 395.79 points or 2.19 percent higher at 18,439.61.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks zigzagged to close higher, shedding some of the morning's gains due to uncertainty over the outlook for property prices in a major government land auction. The Hang Seng Index closed 83.39 points or 0.65 percent higher at 12,832.53.

SYDNEY - Australian stocks closed slightly higher despite a sell-off in bank shares as investors trod cautiously ahead of the rate-setting Federal Open Markets Committee (FOMC) in the United States later today. The All Ordinaries index closed 1.30 points higher at 2,403.40.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended steady in hushed cautious trade as the United States' Federal Open Market Committee met to decide on a possible interest hike. The Overall index ended up 0.6 points to 7,079.5, the Industrial index gained 11.9 points to 8,340.3 and the Gold index made 0.3 points to 1,326.0 points.
